application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript fetch wrapper that provides a higher-level HTTP client API with configurable options, automatic request/response handling, lifecycle hooks, retries, and normalized errors across browser/global and Node.js runtimes.
application.purpose: To make HTTP requests more ergonomic and consistent by wrapping the native fetch API with defaults, query/header merging, body serialization, response parsing, retry behavior, and structured FetchError reporting.

domains.name: Request Execution
domains.description: Core $fetch/$fetchRaw execution flow, including request construction, hook invocation, response parsing, and returning data or raw responses.

domains.name: Options and Headers Resolution
domains.description: Merging default and per-request options, headers, query parameters, and resolving fetch options before execution.

domains.name: Response Processing
domains.description: Detecting response types from content type and parsing body data as JSON, text, blob, arrayBuffer, or stream.

domains.name: Error Handling and Retry
domains.description: Retry policy, retry status codes, timeout/abort handling, and creation of normalized FetchError objects.

domains.name: Runtime Integration
domains.description: Browser/global and Node.js fetch adapters, including optional Node keep-alive agents.

domains.name: Validation and Examples
domains.description: Tests, examples, and playground code that demonstrate or validate fetch behavior.

applicationFacts: The library exposes a main $fetch client and an ofetch alias, with a raw response API available through $fetch.raw.
Request defaults and per-request options are merged, including headers and query/params values.
JSON-serializable request bodies are automatically stringified, and application/json headers are set when appropriate.
Response parsing is inferred from Content-Type unless responseType or parseResponse is provided.
The client supports lifecycle hooks: onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, and onResponseError.
Failed responses can trigger retry logic using configurable retry counts, retry delays, and retry status codes.
Errors are normalized into FetchError objects that expose request, options, response, status, statusText, and parsed data.
A Node-specific entry point provides createNodeFetch and optional keep-alive HTTP/HTTPS agents controlled by FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE.
The build configuration emits declarations and CJS output for src/index and src/node, treating undici as external.
Tests use h3 and listhen to create local HTTP endpoints and validate fetch behavior under Vitest.
